[566](https://docs.rs#566)
[567](https://docs.rs#567)/// Cache operations
[568](https://docs.rs#568)///
[569](https://docs.rs#569)/// ```rust
[570](https://docs.rs#570)/// use cached::{Cached, UnboundCache};
[571](https://docs.rs#571)///
[572](https://docs.rs#572)/// let mut cache: UnboundCache<String, String> = UnboundCache::builder().build().unwrap();
[573](https://docs.rs#573)///
[574](https://docs.rs#574)/// cache.set("key".to_string(), "owned value".to_string());
[575](https://docs.rs#575)///
[576](https://docs.rs#576)/// let borrowed_cache_value = cache.get("key");
[577](https://docs.rs#577)/// assert_eq!(borrowed_cache_value, Some(&"owned value".to_string()))
[578](https://docs.rs#578)/// ```
[579](https://docs.rs#579)pub trait Cached<K, V> {
[580](https://docs.rs#580)    // ── Core required methods (stores implement these) ────────────────────
[581](https://docs.rs#581)
[582](https://docs.rs#582)    /// Attempt to retrieve a cached value.
[583](https://docs.rs#583)    ///
[584](https://docs.rs#584)    /// Takes `&mut self` because some stores update recency, expiration timestamps,
[585](https://docs.rs#585)    /// or metrics during reads.
[586](https://docs.rs#586)    ///
[587](https://docs.rs#587)    /// ```rust
[588](https://docs.rs#588)    /// # use cached::{Cached, UnboundCache};
[589](https://docs.rs#589)    /// # let mut cache: UnboundCache<String, String> = UnboundCache::builder().build().unwrap();
[590](https://docs.rs#590)    /// # cache.set("key".to_string(), "owned value".to_string());
[591](https://docs.rs#591)    /// let v1 = cache.get("key").map(String::clone);
[592](https://docs.rs#592)    /// let v2 = cache.get(&"key".to_string()).map(String::clone);
[593](https://docs.rs#593)    /// # assert_eq!(v1, v2);
[594](https://docs.rs#594)    /// ```
[595](https://docs.rs#595)    fn cache_get<Q>(&mut self, k: &Q) -> Option<&V>
[596](https://docs.rs#596)    where
[597](https://docs.rs#597)        K: std::borrow::Borrow<Q>,
[598](https://docs.rs#598)        Q: std::hash::Hash + Eq + ?Sized;
[599](https://docs.rs#599)
[600](https://docs.rs#600)    /// Attempt to retrieve a cached value with mutable access.
[601](https://docs.rs#601)    fn cache_get_mut<Q>(&mut self, k: &Q) -> Option<&mut V>
[602](https://docs.rs#602)    where
[603](https://docs.rs#603)        K: std::borrow::Borrow<Q>,
[604](https://docs.rs#604)        Q: std::hash::Hash + Eq + ?Sized;
[605](https://docs.rs#605)
[606](https://docs.rs#606)    /// Insert a key-value pair and return the previous value.
[607](https://docs.rs#607)    fn cache_set(&mut self, k: K, v: V) -> Option<V>;
[608](https://docs.rs#608)
[609](https://docs.rs#609)    /// Fallible variant of [`Self::cache_set`]. Returns `Err` if the store cannot accept the entry
[610](https://docs.rs#610)    /// (e.g. the TTL duration overflows `Instant` bounds). The default implementation is
[611](https://docs.rs#611)    /// infallible and delegates to [`Self::cache_set`].
[612](https://docs.rs#612)    fn cache_try_set(&mut self, k: K, v: V) -> Result<Option<V>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
[613](https://docs.rs#613)        Ok(self.cache_set(k, v))
[614](https://docs.rs#614)    }
[615](https://docs.rs#615)
[616](https://docs.rs#616)    /// Get or insert a key-value pair.
[617](https://docs.rs#617)    fn cache_get_or_set_with<F: FnOnce() -> V>(&mut self, key: K, f: F) -> &mut V;
[618](https://docs.rs#618)
[619](https://docs.rs#619)    /// Get or insert a key-value pair, propagating errors from the factory.
[620](https://docs.rs#620)    fn cache_try_get_or_set_with<F: FnOnce() -> Result<V, E>, E>(
[621](https://docs.rs#621)        &mut self,
[622](https://docs.rs#622)        key: K,
[623](https://docs.rs#623)        f: F,
[624](https://docs.rs#624)    ) -> Result<&mut V, E>;
[625](https://docs.rs#625)
[626](https://docs.rs#626)    /// Remove a cached value, returning it if it was both present and still live.
[627](https://docs.rs#627)    ///
[628](https://docs.rs#628)    /// Removing any present entry fires the store's `on_evict` callback (if set) and,
[629](https://docs.rs#629)    /// for stores that track evictions, increments the `evictions` metric consistent
[630](https://docs.rs#630)    /// with automatic eviction. For stores with expiry, an entry that is present but
[631](https://docs.rs#631)    /// already expired is still removed (and still fires `on_evict` / counts as an
[632](https://docs.rs#632)    /// eviction when the store tracks evictions), but `None` is returned because the
[633](https://docs.rs#633)    /// value is no longer valid.
[634](https://docs.rs#634)    ///
[635](https://docs.rs#635)    /// Use [`cache_remove_entry`](Cached::cache_remove_entry) when you need to
[636](https://docs.rs#636)    /// distinguish "key absent" from "key present but expired", or when you need
[637](https://docs.rs#637)    /// the stored key back (relevant when `K`'s `Eq` ignores some fields).
[638](https://docs.rs#638)    ///
[639](https://docs.rs#639)    /// ```rust
[640](https://docs.rs#640)    /// # use cached::{Cached, UnboundCache};
[641](https://docs.rs#641)    /// # let mut cache: UnboundCache<String, String> = UnboundCache::builder().build().unwrap();
[642](https://docs.rs#642)    /// # cache.set("k1".to_string(), "v1".to_string());
[643](https://docs.rs#643)    /// # cache.set("k2".to_string(), "v2".to_string());
[644](https://docs.rs#644)    /// let r1 = cache.remove("k1");
[645](https://docs.rs#645)    /// let r2 = cache.remove(&"k2".to_string());
[646](https://docs.rs#646)    /// # assert_eq!(r1, Some("v1".to_string()));
[647](https://docs.rs#647)    /// # assert_eq!(r2, Some("v2".to_string()));
[648](https://docs.rs#648)    /// ```
[649](https://docs.rs#649)    fn cache_remove<Q>(&mut self, k: &Q) -> Option<V>
[650](https://docs.rs#650)    where
[651](https://docs.rs#651)        K: std::borrow::Borrow<Q>,
[652](https://docs.rs#652)        Q: std::hash::Hash + Eq + ?Sized;
[653](https://docs.rs#653)
[654](https://docs.rs#654)    /// Remove a cached entry, returning the stored key and value whenever an entry
[655](https://docs.rs#655)    /// was physically deleted — including entries that were present but already expired.
[656](https://docs.rs#656)    ///
[657](https://docs.rs#657)    /// This is the key difference from [`cache_remove`](Cached::cache_remove):
[658](https://docs.rs#658)    /// - `cache_remove` returns `None` for both "key absent" and "key present but expired"
[659](https://docs.rs#659)    /// - `cache_remove_entry` returns `Some((stored_key, value))` whenever anything was
[660](https://docs.rs#660)    ///   physically deleted, and `None` only when the key was not in the store at all
[661](https://docs.rs#661)    ///
[662](https://docs.rs#662)    /// This lets callers distinguish between the two cases, and also returns the *stored*
[663](https://docs.rs#663)    /// key rather than the lookup key — relevant when `K`'s `Eq`/`Hash` ignores some
[664](https://docs.rs#664)    /// fields and the stored and lookup instances may differ.
[665](https://docs.rs#665)    ///
[666](https://docs.rs#666)    /// Removing any present entry fires the store's `on_evict` callback (if set) and,
[667](https://docs.rs#667)    /// for stores that track evictions, increments the `evictions` metric.
[668](https://docs.rs#668)    ///
[669](https://docs.rs#669)    /// ```rust
[670](https://docs.rs#670)    /// use cached::{Cached, UnboundCache};
[671](https://docs.rs#671)    ///
[672](https://docs.rs#672)    /// let mut cache: UnboundCache<String, u32> = UnboundCache::builder().build().unwrap();
[673](https://docs.rs#673)    /// cache.cache_set("key".to_string(), 42);
[674](https://docs.rs#674)    ///
[675](https://docs.rs#675)    /// // cache_remove_entry returns Some even for the key that was just inserted.
[676](https://docs.rs#676)    /// let entry = cache.cache_remove_entry("key");
[677](https://docs.rs#677)    /// assert_eq!(entry, Some(("key".to_string(), 42)));
[678](https://docs.rs#678)    ///
[679](https://docs.rs#679)    /// // Returns None only when the key was never present.
[680](https://docs.rs#680)    /// assert_eq!(cache.cache_remove_entry("missing"), None);
[681](https://docs.rs#681)    /// ```
[682](https://docs.rs#682)    fn cache_remove_entry<Q>(&mut self, k: &Q) -> Option<(K, V)>
[683](https://docs.rs#683)    where
[684](https://docs.rs#684)        K: std::borrow::Borrow<Q>,
[685](https://docs.rs#685)        Q: std::hash::Hash + Eq + ?Sized;
[686](https://docs.rs#686)
[687](https://docs.rs#687)    /// Remove all cached entries but preserve capacity allocation and metrics.
[688](https://docs.rs#688)    /// To also reset metrics, call [`cache_reset_metrics`](Cached::cache_reset_metrics) afterward,
[689](https://docs.rs#689)    /// or use [`cache_reset`](Cached::cache_reset) to do both at once.
[690](https://docs.rs#690)    fn cache_clear(&mut self);
[691](https://docs.rs#691)
[692](https://docs.rs#692)    /// Reset all entries and metrics (hits, misses, evictions) to zero.
[693](https://docs.rs#693)    /// Store configuration — capacity, TTL, and `on_evict` callbacks — is preserved.
[694](https://docs.rs#694)    /// To reset entries without resetting metrics, use [`cache_clear`](Cached::cache_clear).
[695](https://docs.rs#695)    fn cache_reset(&mut self);
[696](https://docs.rs#696)
[697](https://docs.rs#697)    /// Return the number of entries currently in the cache.
[698](https://docs.rs#698)    ///
[699](https://docs.rs#699)    /// For stores with TTL-based expiry, this count may include entries that have expired
[700](https://docs.rs#700)    /// but not yet been evicted (lazy eviction).
[701](https://docs.rs#701)    fn cache_size(&self) -> usize;
[702](https://docs.rs#702)
[703](https://docs.rs#703)    // ── Optional overrides ────────────────────────────────────────────────
[704](https://docs.rs#704)
[705](https://docs.rs#705)    /// Reset hit/miss counters.
[706](https://docs.rs#706)    fn cache_reset_metrics(&mut self) {}
[707](https://docs.rs#707)
[708](https://docs.rs#708)    /// Return the number of times a cached value was successfully retrieved.
[709](https://docs.rs#709)    fn cache_hits(&self) -> Option<u64> {
[710](https://docs.rs#710)        None
[711](https://docs.rs#711)    }
[712](https://docs.rs#712)
[713](https://docs.rs#713)    /// Return the number of times a cached value was not found.
[714](https://docs.rs#714)    fn cache_misses(&self) -> Option<u64> {
[715](https://docs.rs#715)        None
[716](https://docs.rs#716)    }
[717](https://docs.rs#717)
[718](https://docs.rs#718)    /// Return the cache capacity, if bounded.
[719](https://docs.rs#719)    fn cache_capacity(&self) -> Option<usize> {
[720](https://docs.rs#720)        None
[721](https://docs.rs#721)    }
[722](https://docs.rs#722)
[723](https://docs.rs#723)    // ── Ergonomic aliases (new preferred API) ────────────────────────────
[724](https://docs.rs#724)
[725](https://docs.rs#725)    /// Retrieve a cached value. Delegates to [`cache_get`](Cached::cache_get).

[732](https://docs.rs#732)    }

[736](https://docs.rs#736)    where
[737](https://docs.rs#737)        K: std::borrow::Borrow<Q>,
[738](https://docs.rs#738)        Q: std::hash::Hash + Eq + ?Sized,
[739](https://docs.rs#739)    {
[740](https://docs.rs#740)        self.cache_get_mut(k)
[741](https://docs.rs#741)    }
[742](https://docs.rs#742)
[743](https://docs.rs#743)    /// Insert a key-value pair and return the previous value. Delegates to [`cache_set`](Cached::cache_set).
[744](https://docs.rs#744)    fn set(&mut self, k: K, v: V) -> Option<V> {
[745](https://docs.rs#745)        self.cache_set(k, v)
[746](https://docs.rs#746)    }

[751](https://docs.rs#751)    }

[786](https://docs.rs#786)    /// Delete a cached entry without returning it. Returns `true` if an entry was
[787](https://docs.rs#787)    /// physically deleted (including expired entries), `false` if the key was absent.
[788](https://docs.rs#788)    ///
[789](https://docs.rs#789)    /// Unlike [`cache_remove`](Cached::cache_remove), this returns `true` even when the
[790](https://docs.rs#790)    /// deleted entry was already expired. Delegates to
[791](https://docs.rs#791)    /// [`cache_remove_entry`](Cached::cache_remove_entry).
[792](https://docs.rs#792)    ///
[793](https://docs.rs#793)    /// ```rust
[794](https://docs.rs#794)    /// use cached::{Cached, UnboundCache};
[795](https://docs.rs#795)    ///
[796](https://docs.rs#796)    /// let mut cache: UnboundCache<String, u32> = UnboundCache::builder().build().unwrap();
[797](https://docs.rs#797)    /// cache.cache_set("key".to_string(), 42);
[798](https://docs.rs#798)    /// assert!(cache.cache_delete("key"));    // present — returns true
[799](https://docs.rs#799)    /// assert!(!cache.cache_delete("key"));   // already gone — returns false
[800](https://docs.rs#800)    /// ```
[801](https://docs.rs#801)    fn cache_delete<Q>(&mut self, k: &Q) -> bool
[802](https://docs.rs#802)    where
[803](https://docs.rs#803)        K: std::borrow::Borrow<Q>,
[804](https://docs.rs#804)        Q: std::hash::Hash + Eq + ?Sized,
[805](https://docs.rs#805)    {
[806](https://docs.rs#806)        self.cache_remove_entry(k).is_some()
[807](https://docs.rs#807)    }
[808](https://docs.rs#808)
[809](https://docs.rs#809)    /// Delete a cached entry without returning it. Returns `true` if an entry was
[810](https://docs.rs#810)    /// physically deleted (including expired entries). Delegates to
[811](https://docs.rs#811)    /// [`cache_delete`](Cached::cache_delete).
[812](https://docs.rs#812)    fn delete<Q>(&mut self, k: &Q) -> bool
[813](https://docs.rs#813)    where
[814](https://docs.rs#814)        K: std::borrow::Borrow<Q>,
[815](https://docs.rs#815)        Q: std::hash::Hash + Eq + ?Sized,
[816](https://docs.rs#816)    {
[817](https://docs.rs#817)        self.cache_delete(k)
[818](https://docs.rs#818)    }
[819](https://docs.rs#819)
[820](https://docs.rs#820)    /// Return `true` if the cache contains a value for the given key.
[821](https://docs.rs#821)    ///
[822](https://docs.rs#822)    /// Requires `&mut self` because some stores update recency, expiration
[823](https://docs.rs#823)    /// timestamps, or metrics during reads. For a non-mutating presence check
[824](https://docs.rs#824)    /// use [`CachedPeek::cache_peek`] if the store implements it.
[825](https://docs.rs#825)    fn contains<Q>(&mut self, k: &Q) -> bool
[826](https://docs.rs#826)    where
[827](https://docs.rs#827)        K: std::borrow::Borrow<Q>,
[828](https://docs.rs#828)        Q: std::hash::Hash + Eq + ?Sized,
[829](https://docs.rs#829)    {
[830](https://docs.rs#830)        self.get(k).is_some()
[831](https://docs.rs#831)    }
[832](https://docs.rs#832)
[833](https://docs.rs#833)    /// Remove all entries, keeping allocated memory for reuse. Delegates to [`cache_clear`](Cached::cache_clear).
[834](https://docs.rs#834)    fn clear(&mut self) {

[836](https://docs.rs#836)    }

[838](https://docs.rs#838)    /// Return the number of entries currently in the cache. Delegates to [`cache_size`](Cached::cache_size).
[839](https://docs.rs#839)    fn len(&self) -> usize {

[922](https://docs.rs#922)impl CacheMetrics {
[923](https://docs.rs#923)    /// Return the cache hit ratio as a value in `[0.0, 1.0]`, or `None` if no lookups have occurred.
[924](https://docs.rs#924)    pub fn hit_ratio(&self) -> Option<f64> {
[925](https://docs.rs#925)        let hits = self.hits?;
[926](https://docs.rs#926)        let misses = self.misses?;
[927](https://docs.rs#927)        let total = hits + misses;
[928](https://docs.rs#928)        if total == 0 {
[929](https://docs.rs#929)            None
[930](https://docs.rs#930)        } else {
[931](https://docs.rs#931)            Some(hits as f64 / total as f64)
[932](https://docs.rs#932)        }
[933](https://docs.rs#933)    }

[936](https://docs.rs#936)/// Non-mutating cache lookup for stores that can expose a value by shared reference.
[937](https://docs.rs#937)///
[938](https://docs.rs#938)/// Peeking does not update recency, refresh TTLs, increment hit/miss metrics, or evict expired
[939](https://docs.rs#939)/// values. It is useful for diagnostics and for implementing read APIs in stores whose normal
[940](https://docs.rs#940)/// lookup semantics do not require recency or refresh mutation.
[941](https://docs.rs#941)pub trait CachedPeek<K, V> {
[942](https://docs.rs#942)    /// Attempt to retrieve a cached value without mutating the cache.

[945](https://docs.rs#945)        K: std::borrow::Borrow<Q>,
[946](https://docs.rs#946)        Q: std::hash::Hash + Eq + ?Sized;
[947](https://docs.rs#947)}
[948](https://docs.rs#948)
[949](https://docs.rs#949)/// Shared-reference cache lookup for stores that can preserve normal read semantics without an
[950](https://docs.rs#950)/// exclusive mutable borrow.
[951](https://docs.rs#951)///
[952](https://docs.rs#952)/// This trait is intentionally narrower than [`CachedPeek`]. Stores with LRU recency updates,
[953](https://docs.rs#953)/// refresh-on-hit TTL behavior, or other read-side mutation should not implement it. Macro-defined
[954](https://docs.rs#954)/// functions use this through `#[cached(unsync_reads = true)]` to take a shared read lock for the
[955](https://docs.rs#955)/// initial cache-hit path while still taking an exclusive write lock for insertion.

[960](https://docs.rs#960)        K: std::borrow::Borrow<Q>,
[961](https://docs.rs#961)        Q: std::hash::Hash + Eq + ?Sized,
[962](https://docs.rs#962)    {
[963](https://docs.rs#963)        self.cache_peek(k)
[964](https://docs.rs#964)    }

[966](https://docs.rs#966)
[967](https://docs.rs#967)/// Extra cache operations for types that implement `Clone`.
[968](https://docs.rs#968)///
[969](https://docs.rs#969)/// [`cache_get_with_expiry_status`](CloneCached::cache_get_with_expiry_status)
[970](https://docs.rs#970)/// returns `(value, expired)` — note an expired entry is still *returned*
[971](https://docs.rs#971)/// (`(Some(v), true)`) so callers can fall back to the stale value if a refresh
[972](https://docs.rs#972)/// fails:
[973](https://docs.rs#973)///
[974](https://docs.rs#974)/// ```rust
[975](https://docs.rs#975)/// # #[cfg(feature = "time_stores")]
[976](https://docs.rs#976)/// # {
[977](https://docs.rs#977)/// use cached::{Cached, CloneCached, TtlCache};
[978](https://docs.rs#978)/// use cached::time::Duration;
[979](https://docs.rs#979)///
[980](https://docs.rs#980)/// let mut c = TtlCache::builder().ttl(Duration::from_secs(60)).build().unwrap();
[981](https://docs.rs#981)/// c.cache_set("k".to_string(), 1);
[982](https://docs.rs#982)/// assert_eq!(c.cache_get_with_expiry_status(&"k".to_string()), (Some(1), false)); // live
[983](https://docs.rs#983)/// assert_eq!(c.cache_get_with_expiry_status(&"x".to_string()), (None, false));    // absent
[984](https://docs.rs#984)/// // (a present-but-expired entry would yield `(Some(v), true)`)
[985](https://docs.rs#985)/// # }
[986](https://docs.rs#986)/// ```
[987](https://docs.rs#987)pub trait CloneCached<K, V> {
[988](https://docs.rs#988)    /// Look up a cached value and report whether the found entry is expired.
[989](https://docs.rs#989)    ///
[990](https://docs.rs#990)    /// Returns `(value, expired)` where:
[991](https://docs.rs#991)    /// - `(None, false)` — key not present
[992](https://docs.rs#992)    /// - `(Some(v), false)` — key present and live
[993](https://docs.rs#993)    /// - `(Some(v), true)` — key present but expired (the stale value is returned so callers
[994](https://docs.rs#994)    ///   can fall back to it if the refresh fails)
[995](https://docs.rs#995)    fn cache_get_with_expiry_status<Q>(&mut self, key: &Q) -> (Option<V>, bool)
[996](https://docs.rs#996)    where
[997](https://docs.rs#997)        K: std::borrow::Borrow<Q>,
[998](https://docs.rs#998)        Q: std::hash::Hash + Eq + ?Sized;
[999](https://docs.rs#999)
[1000](https://docs.rs#1000)    /// Ergonomic alias for [`cache_get_with_expiry_status`](Self::cache_get_with_expiry_status).
[1001](https://docs.rs#1001)    fn get_with_expiry_status<Q>(&mut self, key: &Q) -> (Option<V>, bool)
[1002](https://docs.rs#1002)    where
[1003](https://docs.rs#1003)        K: std::borrow::Borrow<Q>,
[1004](https://docs.rs#1004)        Q: std::hash::Hash + Eq + ?Sized,
[1005](https://docs.rs#1005)    {
[1006](https://docs.rs#1006)        self.cache_get_with_expiry_status(key)
[1007](https://docs.rs#1007)    }
[1008](https://docs.rs#1008)}
[1009](https://docs.rs#1009)
[1010](https://docs.rs#1010)/// Concurrent analogue of [`CloneCached`] for the internally-synchronized sharded stores.
[1011](https://docs.rs#1011)///
[1012](https://docs.rs#1012)/// Like [`CloneCached`], [`cache_get_with_expiry_status`](ConcurrentCloneCached::cache_get_with_expiry_status)
[1013](https://docs.rs#1013)/// returns a present-but-expired entry **without removing it**, so callers (e.g.
[1014](https://docs.rs#1014)/// [`result_fallback`](macro@crate::macros::concurrent_cached)) can fall back to the stale
[1015](https://docs.rs#1015)/// value if a refresh fails. Takes `&self` instead of `&mut self` because sharded stores are
[1016](https://docs.rs#1016)/// internally synchronized and never need exclusive ownership from the caller.
[1017](https://docs.rs#1017)///
[1018](https://docs.rs#1018)/// Implemented by the four expiry-capable sharded stores:
[1019](https://docs.rs#1019)/// [`ShardedTtlCache`], [`ShardedLruTtlCache`], [`ShardedExpiringCache`], and
[1020](https://docs.rs#1020)/// [`ShardedExpiringLruCache`].
[1021](https://docs.rs#1021)/// Non-expiry stores ([`ShardedCache`], [`ShardedLruCache`]) do not implement this trait,
[1022](https://docs.rs#1022)/// mirroring how [`CloneCached`] is absent on [`UnboundCache`] and [`LruCache`].
[1023](https://docs.rs#1023)///
[1024](https://docs.rs#1024)/// **Why `&K` instead of `&Q` (`Borrow<Q>`)**: same reason as [`ConcurrentCached`] — the
[1025](https://docs.rs#1025)/// concurrent cache trait family includes external stores that must serialize the key, so
[1026](https://docs.rs#1026)/// the trait takes `&K` directly rather than a generic `Borrow<Q>` that carries no
[1027](https://docs.rs#1027)/// serialization guarantee.
[1028](https://docs.rs#1028)///
[1029](https://docs.rs#1029)/// **Race window**: between the expiry check and the subsequent re-cache on `Err`, another
[1030](https://docs.rs#1030)/// thread may have stored a fresh `Ok`. The re-cache will overwrite that fresh value, but
[1031](https://docs.rs#1031)/// the outcome is only a redundant function call on the next expiry — not data corruption.
[1032](https://docs.rs#1032)///
[1033](https://docs.rs#1033)/// # Examples
[1034](https://docs.rs#1034)///
[1035](https://docs.rs#1035)/// ```rust
[1036](https://docs.rs#1036)/// # #[cfg(feature = "time_stores")]
[1037](https://docs.rs#1037)/// # {
[1038](https://docs.rs#1038)/// use cached::{ConcurrentCached, ConcurrentCloneCached, ShardedTtlCache};
[1039](https://docs.rs#1039)/// use cached::time::Duration;
[1040](https://docs.rs#1040)///
[1041](https://docs.rs#1041)/// let c = ShardedTtlCache::builder().ttl(Duration::from_secs(60)).build().unwrap();
[1042](https://docs.rs#1042)/// c.cache_set("k".to_string(), 1_i32).expect("infallible ShardedTtlCache set");
[1043](https://docs.rs#1043)/// assert_eq!(c.cache_get_with_expiry_status(&"k".to_string()), (Some(1_i32), false)); // live
[1044](https://docs.rs#1044)/// assert_eq!(c.cache_get_with_expiry_status(&"x".to_string()), (None, false));        // absent
[1045](https://docs.rs#1045)/// // a present-but-expired entry yields (Some(v), true)
[1046](https://docs.rs#1046)/// # }
[1047](https://docs.rs#1047)/// ```
[1048](https://docs.rs#1048)pub trait ConcurrentCloneCached<K, V> {
[1049](https://docs.rs#1049)    /// Look up a cached value and report whether the found entry is expired.
[1050](https://docs.rs#1050)    ///
[1051](https://docs.rs#1051)    /// Returns `(value, expired)` where:
[1052](https://docs.rs#1052)    /// - `(None, false)` — key not present
[1053](https://docs.rs#1053)    /// - `(Some(v), false)` — key present and live (hits counter incremented)
[1054](https://docs.rs#1054)    /// - `(Some(v), true)` — key present but expired; the stale value is returned so callers
[1055](https://docs.rs#1055)    ///   can fall back to it if a refresh fails. The entry is **not** removed from the cache
[1056](https://docs.rs#1056)    ///   and eviction counters are **not** incremented (misses counter incremented).
[1057](https://docs.rs#1057)    ///
[1058](https://docs.rs#1058)    /// Unlike [`ConcurrentCached::cache_get`], this never removes an expired entry — it
[1059](https://docs.rs#1059)    /// intentionally leaves it in place so it can be returned as a stale fallback. Expired
[1060](https://docs.rs#1060)    /// entries are swept by a subsequent `cache_get`, an explicit `cache_remove`, or `evict()`.
[1061](https://docs.rs#1061)    fn cache_get_with_expiry_status(&self, key: &K) -> (Option<V>, bool);
[1062](https://docs.rs#1062)}
[1063](https://docs.rs#1063)
[1064](https://docs.rs#1064)/// TTL management for time-bounded cache stores.
[1065](https://docs.rs#1065)///
[1066](https://docs.rs#1066)/// Implemented by [`TtlCache`], [`LruTtlCache`], [`TtlSortedCache`],
[1067](https://docs.rs#1067)/// [`ShardedTtlCache`], [`ShardedLruTtlCache`], [`RedisCache`], and [`DiskCache`].
[1068](https://docs.rs#1068)///
[1069](https://docs.rs#1069)/// This trait requires the `time_stores` feature. `DiskCache` implements it only when
[1070](https://docs.rs#1070)/// both `disk_store` and `time_stores` features are enabled.
[1071](https://docs.rs#1071)///
[1072](https://docs.rs#1072)/// > **Note for `DiskCache` users**: if you disable the `default` feature set and
[1073](https://docs.rs#1073)/// > enable only `disk_store`, the `time_stores` feature will not be present and
[1074](https://docs.rs#1074)/// > `DiskCache` will not implement this trait — `set_ttl`, `ttl`, and related methods
[1075](https://docs.rs#1075)/// > will be unavailable. Re-enable `time_stores` (or use the `default` feature set)
[1076](https://docs.rs#1076)/// > to restore them.
[1077](https://docs.rs#1077)#[cfg(feature = "time_stores")]
[1078](https://docs.rs#1078)#[cfg_attr(docsrs, doc(cfg(feature = "time_stores")))]
[1079](https://docs.rs#1079)pub trait CacheTtl {
[1080](https://docs.rs#1080)    /// Return the TTL applied to newly inserted entries.
[1081](https://docs.rs#1081)    fn ttl(&self) -> Option<Duration>;
[1082](https://docs.rs#1082)
[1083](https://docs.rs#1083)    /// Set the TTL for newly inserted entries, returning the previous value.
[1084](https://docs.rs#1084)    ///
[1085](https://docs.rs#1085)    /// # Panics
[1086](https://docs.rs#1086)    ///
[1087](https://docs.rs#1087)    /// Implementations that accept a TTL panic if `ttl.is_zero()` — use
[1088](https://docs.rs#1088)    /// [`unset_ttl`](Self::unset_ttl) to disable expiry instead.
[1089](https://docs.rs#1089)    fn set_ttl(&mut self, ttl: Duration) -> Option<Duration>;
[1090](https://docs.rs#1090)
[1091](https://docs.rs#1091)    /// Remove the TTL so entries are retained indefinitely.
[1092](https://docs.rs#1092)    ///
[1093](https://docs.rs#1093)    /// No-op for stores that cannot retain values indefinitely.
[1094](https://docs.rs#1094)    fn unset_ttl(&mut self) -> Option<Duration>;
[1095](https://docs.rs#1095)
[1096](https://docs.rs#1096)    /// Return `true` if cache hits refresh the TTL of the accessed entry.
[1097](https://docs.rs#1097)    fn refresh_on_hit(&self) -> bool {
[1098](https://docs.rs#1098)        false
[1099](https://docs.rs#1099)    }
[1100](https://docs.rs#1100)
[1101](https://docs.rs#1101)    /// Set whether cache hits should refresh the TTL. Returns the previous value.
[1102](https://docs.rs#1102)    fn set_refresh_on_hit(&mut self, _refresh: bool) -> bool {
[1103](https://docs.rs#1103)        false
[1104](https://docs.rs#1104)    }

[1106](https://docs.rs#1106)
[1107](https://docs.rs#1107)#[cfg(feature = "async_core")]
[1108](https://docs.rs#1108)#[cfg_attr(docsrs, doc(cfg(feature = "async_core")))]
[1109](https://docs.rs#1109)pub trait CachedAsync<K, V> {
[1110](https://docs.rs#1110)    /// Get the value for `k`, or compute and insert it by awaiting `f` on a miss.
[1111](https://docs.rs#1111)    ///
[1112](https://docs.rs#1112)    /// The async counterpart of [`Cached::get_or_set_with`]. It is `async_`-prefixed
[1113](https://docs.rs#1113)    /// so that importing both [`Cached`] and [`CachedAsync`] (common, since the
[1114](https://docs.rs#1114)    /// in-memory stores implement both) does not make `get_or_set_with` ambiguous
[1115](https://docs.rs#1115)    /// at the call site.
[1116](https://docs.rs#1116)    fn async_get_or_set_with<'a, F, Fut>(
[1117](https://docs.rs#1117)        &'a mut self,
[1118](https://docs.rs#1118)        k: K,
[1119](https://docs.rs#1119)        f: F,
[1120](https://docs.rs#1120)    ) -> impl Future<Output = &'a mut V> + Send + 'a
[1121](https://docs.rs#1121)    where
[1122](https://docs.rs#1122)        K: 'a,
[1123](https://docs.rs#1123)        V: Send + 'a,
[1124](https://docs.rs#1124)        F: FnOnce() -> Fut + Send + 'a,
[1125](https://docs.rs#1125)        Fut: Future<Output = V> + Send + 'a;
[1126](https://docs.rs#1126)
[1127](https://docs.rs#1127)    /// Like [`async_get_or_set_with`](CachedAsync::async_get_or_set_with), but
[1128](https://docs.rs#1128)    /// `f` is fallible: on a miss the value is cached only if `f` resolves to
[1129](https://docs.rs#1129)    /// `Ok`, and an `Err` is returned without caching.
[1130](https://docs.rs#1130)    fn async_try_get_or_set_with<'a, F, Fut, E>(
[1131](https://docs.rs#1131)        &'a mut self,
[1132](https://docs.rs#1132)        k: K,
[1133](https://docs.rs#1133)        f: F,
[1134](https://docs.rs#1134)    ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<&'a mut V, E>> + Send + 'a
[1135](https://docs.rs#1135)    where
[1136](https://docs.rs#1136)        K: 'a,
[1137](https://docs.rs#1137)        V: Send + 'a,
[1138](https://docs.rs#1138)        E: 'a,
[1139](https://docs.rs#1139)        F: FnOnce() -> Fut + Send + 'a,
[1140](https://docs.rs#1140)        Fut: Future<Output = Result<V, E>> + Send + 'a;
[1141](https://docs.rs#1141)
[1142](https://docs.rs#1142)    /// Retrieve a cached value asynchronously.
[1143](https://docs.rs#1143)    ///
[1144](https://docs.rs#1144)    /// Defaults to calling the synchronous [`Cached::cache_get`] implementation. Stores can
[1145](https://docs.rs#1145)    /// override to provide a truly async path.
[1146](https://docs.rs#1146)    fn get_async<'a, Q>(&'a mut self, k: &'a Q) -> impl Future<Output = Option<&'a V>> + Send + 'a
[1147](https://docs.rs#1147)    where
[1148](https://docs.rs#1148)        Self: Cached<K, V> + Send,
[1149](https://docs.rs#1149)        K: std::borrow::Borrow<Q> + 'a,
[1150](https://docs.rs#1150)        Q: std::hash::Hash + Eq + ?Sized + Sync,
[1151](https://docs.rs#1151)        V: 'a,
[1152](https://docs.rs#1152)    {
[1153](https://docs.rs#1153)        async move { self.get(k) }
[1154](https://docs.rs#1154)    }
[1155](https://docs.rs#1155)
[1156](https://docs.rs#1156)    /// Insert a key-value pair asynchronously.
[1157](https://docs.rs#1157)    ///
[1158](https://docs.rs#1158)    /// Defaults to calling the synchronous [`Cached::cache_set`] implementation.
[1159](https://docs.rs#1159)    fn set_async(&mut self, k: K, v: V) -> impl Future<Output = Option<V>> + Send
[1160](https://docs.rs#1160)    where
[1161](https://docs.rs#1161)        Self: Cached<K, V> + Send,
[1162](https://docs.rs#1162)        K: Send,
[1163](https://docs.rs#1163)        V: Send,
[1164](https://docs.rs#1164)    {
[1165](https://docs.rs#1165)        async move { self.set(k, v) }
[1166](https://docs.rs#1166)    }
[1167](https://docs.rs#1167)
[1168](https://docs.rs#1168)    /// Remove a cached value asynchronously.
[1169](https://docs.rs#1169)    ///
[1170](https://docs.rs#1170)    /// Defaults to calling the synchronous [`Cached::cache_remove`] implementation.
[1171](https://docs.rs#1171)    fn remove_async<'a, Q>(&'a mut self, k: &'a Q) -> impl Future<Output = Option<V>> + Send + 'a
[1172](https://docs.rs#1172)    where
[1173](https://docs.rs#1173)        Self: Cached<K, V> + Send,
[1174](https://docs.rs#1174)        K: std::borrow::Borrow<Q> + 'a,
[1175](https://docs.rs#1175)        Q: std::hash::Hash + Eq + ?Sized + Sync,
[1176](https://docs.rs#1176)        V: 'a,
[1177](https://docs.rs#1177)    {
[1178](https://docs.rs#1178)        async move { self.remove(k) }
[1179](https://docs.rs#1179)    }
[1180](https://docs.rs#1180)
[1181](https://docs.rs#1181)    /// Remove all entries asynchronously.
[1182](https://docs.rs#1182)    ///
[1183](https://docs.rs#1183)    /// Defaults to calling the synchronous [`Cached::cache_clear`] implementation.
[1184](https://docs.rs#1184)    fn clear_async(&mut self) -> impl Future<Output = ()> + Send
[1185](https://docs.rs#1185)    where
[1186](https://docs.rs#1186)        Self: Cached<K, V> + Send,
[1187](https://docs.rs#1187)    {
[1188](https://docs.rs#1188)        async move { self.clear() }
[1189](https://docs.rs#1189)    }
[1190](https://docs.rs#1190)}
[1191](https://docs.rs#1191)
[1192](https://docs.rs#1192)/// Cache operations on a store that manages its own synchronization (a shared,
[1193](https://docs.rs#1193)/// `&self` API with owned return values and a fallible `Error`). Implemented by
[1194](https://docs.rs#1194)/// `RedisCache`/`DiskCache`; implement it directly for a custom concurrent or
[1195](https://docs.rs#1195)/// IO-backed store (this is the ~10-line pattern the 1.0 migration guide
[1196](https://docs.rs#1196)/// recommends in place of the removed `InMemoryAdapter`):
[1197](https://docs.rs#1197)///
[1198](https://docs.rs#1198)/// ```rust
[1199](https://docs.rs#1199)/// use cached::ConcurrentCached;
[1200](https://docs.rs#1200)/// use std::collections::HashMap;
[1201](https://docs.rs#1201)/// use std::sync::Mutex;
[1202](https://docs.rs#1202)///
[1203](https://docs.rs#1203)/// struct MyStore(Mutex<HashMap<String, u32>>);
[1204](https://docs.rs#1204)///
[1205](https://docs.rs#1205)/// impl ConcurrentCached<String, u32> for MyStore {
[1206](https://docs.rs#1206)///     type Error = std::convert::Infallible;
[1207](https://docs.rs#1207)///     fn cache_get(&self, k: &String) -> Result<Option<u32>, Self::Error> {
[1208](https://docs.rs#1208)///         Ok(self.0.lock().unwrap().get(k).copied())
[1209](https://docs.rs#1209)///     }
[1210](https://docs.rs#1210)///     fn cache_set(&self, k: String, v: u32) -> Result<Option<u32>, Self::Error> {
[1211](https://docs.rs#1211)///         Ok(self.0.lock().unwrap().insert(k, v))
[1212](https://docs.rs#1212)///     }
[1213](https://docs.rs#1213)///     fn cache_remove(&self, k: &String) -> Result<Option<u32>, Self::Error> {
[1214](https://docs.rs#1214)///         Ok(self.0.lock().unwrap().remove(k))
[1215](https://docs.rs#1215)///     }
[1216](https://docs.rs#1216)///     fn cache_remove_entry(&self, k: &String) -> Result<Option<(String, u32)>, Self::Error> {
[1217](https://docs.rs#1217)///         Ok(self.0.lock().unwrap().remove_entry(k))
[1218](https://docs.rs#1218)///     }
[1219](https://docs.rs#1219)///     fn set_refresh_on_hit(&self, _refresh: bool) -> bool { false }
[1220](https://docs.rs#1220)/// }
[1221](https://docs.rs#1221)///
[1222](https://docs.rs#1222)/// let store = MyStore(Mutex::new(HashMap::new()));
[1223](https://docs.rs#1223)/// assert_eq!(store.cache_get(&"k".to_string()).expect("MyStore is infallible"), None);
[1224](https://docs.rs#1224)/// assert_eq!(store.cache_set("k".to_string(), 7).expect("MyStore is infallible"), None);
[1225](https://docs.rs#1225)/// assert_eq!(store.cache_get(&"k".to_string()).expect("MyStore is infallible"), Some(7));
[1226](https://docs.rs#1226)/// assert_eq!(store.cache_remove(&"k".to_string()).expect("MyStore is infallible"), Some(7));
[1227](https://docs.rs#1227)/// ```
[1228](https://docs.rs#1228)/// **Direct-call syntax warning**:
[1229](https://docs.rs#1229)///
[1230](https://docs.rs#1230)/// Both `ConcurrentCached` and `ConcurrentCachedAsync` define identical method names for their core
[1231](https://docs.rs#1231)/// operations (`cache_get`, `cache_set`, `cache_remove`, `cache_delete`). Sharded in-memory stores
[1232](https://docs.rs#1232)/// also expose synchronous inherent helpers with those names, so method-call syntax on a sharded
[1233](https://docs.rs#1233)/// store resolves to the sync helper even if only `ConcurrentCachedAsync` is imported.
[1234](https://docs.rs#1234)///
[1235](https://docs.rs#1235)/// To resolve this, use Universal Function Call Syntax (UFCS) when calling these methods manually:
[1236](https://docs.rs#1236)/// ```rust,ignore
[1237](https://docs.rs#1237)/// ::cached::ConcurrentCached::cache_get(&cache, &key)
[1238](https://docs.rs#1238)/// ```
[1239](https://docs.rs#1239)///
[1240](https://docs.rs#1240)/// **Why key-lookup methods take `&K` instead of `&Q` (`Borrow<Q>`)**:
[1241](https://docs.rs#1241)///
[1242](https://docs.rs#1242)/// [`Cached`] uses `Borrow<Q>` for all key-lookup methods (e.g. look up a `String` key with a
[1243](https://docs.rs#1243)/// `&str`). `ConcurrentCached` cannot follow the same pattern because its implementors include
[1244](https://docs.rs#1244)/// external stores (`DiskCache`, `RedisCache`) that must *serialize* the key in order to perform
[1245](https://docs.rs#1245)/// a lookup. A generic `&Q` where only `K: Borrow<Q>` carries no serialization guarantee, and
[1246](https://docs.rs#1246)/// adding a `Q: Serialize` bound to the trait would bleed a serde dependency into every
[1247](https://docs.rs#1247)/// `ConcurrentCached` implementation. All key-lookup methods therefore take `&K` directly.
[1248](https://docs.rs#1248)pub trait ConcurrentCached<K, V> {
[1249](https://docs.rs#1249)    type Error;
[1250](https://docs.rs#1250)
[1251](https://docs.rs#1251)    /// Attempt to retrieve a cached value
[1252](https://docs.rs#1252)    ///
[1253](https://docs.rs#1253)    /// # Errors
[1254](https://docs.rs#1254)    ///
[1255](https://docs.rs#1255)    /// Should return `Self::Error` if the operation fails
[1256](https://docs.rs#1256)    fn cache_get(&self, k: &K) -> Result<Option<V>, Self::Error>;
[1257](https://docs.rs#1257)
[1258](https://docs.rs#1258)    /// Insert a key, value pair and return the previous value at the key, if any,
[1259](https://docs.rs#1259)    /// without checking expiry. For TTL-based stores the returned value may have
[1260](https://docs.rs#1260)    /// elapsed its TTL; for per-value expiry stores (implementing [`Expires`]) the
[1261](https://docs.rs#1261)    /// returned value may report `is_expired() == true`. Check expiry on the returned
[1262](https://docs.rs#1262)    /// value if you need to distinguish a live previous entry from an expired one.
[1263](https://docs.rs#1263)    ///
[1264](https://docs.rs#1264)    /// # Errors
[1265](https://docs.rs#1265)    ///
[1266](https://docs.rs#1266)    /// Should return `Self::Error` if the operation fails
[1267](https://docs.rs#1267)    fn cache_set(&self, k: K, v: V) -> Result<Option<V>, Self::Error>;
[1268](https://docs.rs#1268)
[1269](https://docs.rs#1269)    /// Remove a cached value, returning it if it was both present and still live.
[1270](https://docs.rs#1270)    ///
[1271](https://docs.rs#1271)    /// For stores with expiry, an entry that is present but already expired is still
[1272](https://docs.rs#1272)    /// removed (and fires `on_evict` / counts an eviction), but `None` is returned.
[1273](https://docs.rs#1273)    /// Use [`cache_remove_entry`](ConcurrentCached::cache_remove_entry) when you need
[1274](https://docs.rs#1274)    /// to distinguish "key absent" from "key present but expired".
[1275](https://docs.rs#1275)    ///
[1276](https://docs.rs#1276)    /// # Errors
[1277](https://docs.rs#1277)    ///
[1278](https://docs.rs#1278)    /// Should return `Self::Error` if the operation fails
[1279](https://docs.rs#1279)    fn cache_remove(&self, k: &K) -> Result<Option<V>, Self::Error>;
[1280](https://docs.rs#1280)
[1281](https://docs.rs#1281)    /// Remove a cached entry, returning the stored key and value whenever an entry
[1282](https://docs.rs#1282)    /// was physically deleted — including entries that were present but already expired.
[1283](https://docs.rs#1283)    ///
[1284](https://docs.rs#1284)    /// This is the key difference from [`cache_remove`](ConcurrentCached::cache_remove):
[1285](https://docs.rs#1285)    /// - `cache_remove` returns `None` for both "key absent" and "key present but expired"
[1286](https://docs.rs#1286)    /// - `cache_remove_entry` returns `Some((stored_key, value))` whenever anything was
[1287](https://docs.rs#1287)    ///   physically deleted, and `None` only when the key was not in the store at all
[1288](https://docs.rs#1288)    ///
[1289](https://docs.rs#1289)    /// This expired-but-present guarantee holds for the in-memory stores (sharded and
[1290](https://docs.rs#1290)    /// non-sharded). Stores that enforce TTL server-side — `RedisCache` / `AsyncRedisCache` —
[1291](https://docs.rs#1291)    /// cannot read the value of a TTL-expired key and so return `None` for it, exactly like
[1292](https://docs.rs#1292)    /// `cache_remove`; see ["Note on Redis and external stores"](#note-on-redis-and-external-stores)
[1293](https://docs.rs#1293)    /// below.
[1294](https://docs.rs#1294)    ///
[1295](https://docs.rs#1295)    /// Removing any present entry fires the store's `on_evict` callback (if set) and,
[1296](https://docs.rs#1296)    /// for stores that track evictions, increments the `evictions` metric.
[1297](https://docs.rs#1297)    ///
[1298](https://docs.rs#1298)    /// # Note on `K: Clone`
[1299](https://docs.rs#1299)    ///
[1300](https://docs.rs#1300)    /// Implementations that reconstruct the stored key from the lookup key — such as
[1301](https://docs.rs#1301)    /// `DiskCache` and `RedisCache` — require `K: Clone` to produce the stored-key half
[1302](https://docs.rs#1302)    /// of the returned tuple.  Sharded in-memory stores return the physically stored key
[1303](https://docs.rs#1303)    /// and do not impose this bound.
[1304](https://docs.rs#1304)    ///
[1305](https://docs.rs#1305)    /// # Note on Redis and external stores
[1306](https://docs.rs#1306)    ///
[1307](https://docs.rs#1307)    /// Stores that enforce TTL server-side (e.g. `RedisCache`, `AsyncRedisCache`) cannot
[1308](https://docs.rs#1308)    /// retrieve the value of a TTL-expired key — `GET` returns nil once the TTL elapses,
[1309](https://docs.rs#1309)    /// even before the background expiry sweep removes the key.  For such stores,
[1310](https://docs.rs#1310)    /// `cache_remove_entry` behaves identically to `cache_remove` and returns `None` for
[1311](https://docs.rs#1311)    /// server-side-expired entries.  Use [`cache_delete`](ConcurrentCached::cache_delete)
[1312](https://docs.rs#1312)    /// (which issues `DEL` directly) to reliably confirm whether any physical entry was removed.
[1313](https://docs.rs#1313)    ///
[1314](https://docs.rs#1314)    /// # Errors
[1315](https://docs.rs#1315)    ///
[1316](https://docs.rs#1316)    /// Should return `Self::Error` if the operation fails
[1317](https://docs.rs#1317)    ///
[1318](https://docs.rs#1318)    /// # Example
[1319](https://docs.rs#1319)    ///
[1320](https://docs.rs#1320)    /// ```rust
[1321](https://docs.rs#1321)    /// use cached::{ConcurrentCached, ShardedCache};
[1322](https://docs.rs#1322)    ///
[1323](https://docs.rs#1323)    /// let cache: ShardedCache<String, u32> = ShardedCache::builder().build().unwrap();
[1324](https://docs.rs#1324)    /// cache.cache_set("key".to_string(), 42).expect("ShardedCache is infallible");
[1325](https://docs.rs#1325)    ///
[1326](https://docs.rs#1326)    /// // cache_remove_entry always returns Some when the key was present.
[1327](https://docs.rs#1327)    /// let entry = cache.cache_remove_entry(&"key".to_string()).expect("ShardedCache is infallible");
[1328](https://docs.rs#1328)    /// assert_eq!(entry, Some(("key".to_string(), 42)));
[1329](https://docs.rs#1329)    ///
[1330](https://docs.rs#1330)    /// // Returns None only when the key was never present.
[1331](https://docs.rs#1331)    /// assert_eq!(cache.cache_remove_entry(&"missing".to_string()).expect("ShardedCache is infallible"), None);
[1332](https://docs.rs#1332)    /// ```
[1333](https://docs.rs#1333)    fn cache_remove_entry(&self, k: &K) -> Result<Option<(K, V)>, Self::Error>;
[1334](https://docs.rs#1334)
[1335](https://docs.rs#1335)    /// Delete a cached value without returning or decoding the stored value.
[1336](https://docs.rs#1336)    ///
[1337](https://docs.rs#1337)    /// Returns `true` if an entry (live or expired) was physically removed from the
[1338](https://docs.rs#1338)    /// store, `false` if the key was not present. This differs from the 1.x
[1339](https://docs.rs#1339)    /// behaviour where `cache_delete` returned `false` for expired entries — use
[1340](https://docs.rs#1340)    /// [`cache_remove`](ConcurrentCached::cache_remove) if you need to distinguish
[1341](https://docs.rs#1341)    /// a live removal from an expired one.
[1342](https://docs.rs#1342)    ///
[1343](https://docs.rs#1343)    /// # Errors
[1344](https://docs.rs#1344)    ///
[1345](https://docs.rs#1345)    /// Should return `Self::Error` if the operation fails
[1346](https://docs.rs#1346)    fn cache_delete(&self, k: &K) -> Result<bool, Self::Error> {
[1347](https://docs.rs#1347)        self.cache_remove_entry(k).map(|removed| removed.is_some())
[1348](https://docs.rs#1348)    }
[1349](https://docs.rs#1349)
[1350](https://docs.rs#1350)    /// Retrieve a cached value. Delegates to [`cache_get`](ConcurrentCached::cache_get).
[1351](https://docs.rs#1351)    #[inline]
[1352](https://docs.rs#1352)    fn get(&self, k: &K) -> Result<Option<V>, Self::Error> {
[1353](https://docs.rs#1353)        self.cache_get(k)
[1354](https://docs.rs#1354)    }
[1355](https://docs.rs#1355)
[1356](https://docs.rs#1356)    /// Insert a key-value pair and return the previous value. Delegates to [`cache_set`](ConcurrentCached::cache_set).
[1357](https://docs.rs#1357)    #[inline]
[1358](https://docs.rs#1358)    fn set(&self, k: K, v: V) -> Result<Option<V>, Self::Error> {
[1359](https://docs.rs#1359)        self.cache_set(k, v)
[1360](https://docs.rs#1360)    }
[1361](https://docs.rs#1361)
[1362](https://docs.rs#1362)    /// Remove a cached value and return it. Delegates to [`cache_remove`](ConcurrentCached::cache_remove).
[1363](https://docs.rs#1363)    #[inline]
[1364](https://docs.rs#1364)    fn remove(&self, k: &K) -> Result<Option<V>, Self::Error> {
[1365](https://docs.rs#1365)        self.cache_remove(k)
[1366](https://docs.rs#1366)    }
[1367](https://docs.rs#1367)
[1368](https://docs.rs#1368)    /// Remove a cached entry and return the stored key and value. Delegates to [`cache_remove_entry`](ConcurrentCached::cache_remove_entry).
[1369](https://docs.rs#1369)    #[inline]
[1370](https://docs.rs#1370)    fn remove_entry(&self, k: &K) -> Result<Option<(K, V)>, Self::Error> {
[1371](https://docs.rs#1371)        self.cache_remove_entry(k)
[1372](https://docs.rs#1372)    }
[1373](https://docs.rs#1373)
[1374](https://docs.rs#1374)    /// Delete a cached value without returning it. Delegates to [`cache_delete`](ConcurrentCached::cache_delete).
[1375](https://docs.rs#1375)    #[inline]
[1376](https://docs.rs#1376)    fn delete(&self, k: &K) -> Result<bool, Self::Error> {
[1377](https://docs.rs#1377)        self.cache_delete(k)
[1378](https://docs.rs#1378)    }
[1379](https://docs.rs#1379)
[1380](https://docs.rs#1380)    /// Report the number of entries currently held by the store, if the store can
[1381](https://docs.rs#1381)    /// determine it cheaply.
[1382](https://docs.rs#1382)    ///
[1383](https://docs.rs#1383)    /// Returns `Ok(Some(n))` for stores that track their own size (all in-memory sharded
[1384](https://docs.rs#1384)    /// stores), and `Ok(None)` for stores that cannot answer without an expensive or
[1385](https://docs.rs#1385)    /// semantically-ambiguous query — `RedisCache` / `AsyncRedisCache` (the key count is a
[1386](https://docs.rs#1386)    /// server-side `DBSIZE`/`SCAN` over a shared keyspace, not just this cache's entries) and
[1387](https://docs.rs#1387)    /// `DiskCache` (an `O(n)` scan of the backing tree). Those stores return `Ok(None)` rather
[1388](https://docs.rs#1388)    /// than pay that cost implicitly; query the backend directly if you need their size.
[1389](https://docs.rs#1389)    ///
[1390](https://docs.rs#1390)    /// This is the concurrent analogue of [`Cached::cache_size`], widened to
[1391](https://docs.rs#1391)    /// `Result<Option<usize>, _>` because concurrent stores may be fallible and may not know
[1392](https://docs.rs#1392)    /// their size. The default returns `Ok(None)`.
[1393](https://docs.rs#1393)    ///
[1394](https://docs.rs#1394)    /// # Errors
[1395](https://docs.rs#1395)    ///
[1396](https://docs.rs#1396)    /// Should return `Self::Error` if determining the size fails.
[1397](https://docs.rs#1397)    fn cache_size(&self) -> Result<Option<usize>, Self::Error> {
[1398](https://docs.rs#1398)        Ok(None)
[1399](https://docs.rs#1399)    }
[1400](https://docs.rs#1400)

[1411](https://docs.rs#1411)    }
[1412](https://docs.rs#1412)

[1417](https://docs.rs#1417)    fn set_ttl(&self, _ttl: Duration) -> Option<Duration> {

[1419](https://docs.rs#1419)    }

[1431](https://docs.rs#1431)/// **Direct-call syntax warning**:
[1432](https://docs.rs#1432)///
[1433](https://docs.rs#1433)/// Both `ConcurrentCached` and `ConcurrentCachedAsync` define identical method names for their core
[1434](https://docs.rs#1434)/// operations (`cache_get`, `cache_set`, `cache_remove`, `cache_delete`). Sharded in-memory stores
[1435](https://docs.rs#1435)/// also expose synchronous inherent helpers with those names, so method-call syntax on a sharded
[1436](https://docs.rs#1436)/// store resolves to the sync helper even if only `ConcurrentCachedAsync` is imported.
[1437](https://docs.rs#1437)///
[1438](https://docs.rs#1438)/// To resolve this, use Universal Function Call Syntax (UFCS) when calling these methods manually:
[1439](https://docs.rs#1439)/// ```rust,ignore
[1440](https://docs.rs#1440)/// ::cached::ConcurrentCachedAsync::cache_get(&cache, &key).await
[1441](https://docs.rs#1441)/// ```
[1442](https://docs.rs#1442)///
[1443](https://docs.rs#1443)/// **Short aliases not provided**: Unlike [`ConcurrentCached`], this trait intentionally does
[1444](https://docs.rs#1444)/// **not** expose `get`/`set`/`remove`/`delete` short aliases. Adding them would worsen the
[1445](https://docs.rs#1445)/// method-resolution ambiguity described above: a sharded store that implements both sync and
[1446](https://docs.rs#1446)/// async concurrent traits would then have colliding inherent helpers and two sets of alias
[1447](https://docs.rs#1447)/// defaults, making UFCS mandatory even for the aliases.
[1448](https://docs.rs#1448)#[cfg(feature = "async_core")]
[1449](https://docs.rs#1449)#[cfg_attr(docsrs, doc(cfg(feature = "async_core")))]

# ShardHasher in cached::stores::sharded - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cached/2.0.2/cached/stores/sharded/trait.ShardHasher.html

```
pub trait ShardHasher<K>:

```
[Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html)
    + [Sync](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sync.html)
    + 'static {
    // Required method
    fn [shard_hash](https://docs.rs#tymethod.shard_hash)(&self, key: [&K](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)) -> [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html);
}## Expand description

Trait for types that deterministically map a key to a `u64` shard hash.

No `K: Hash` bound on the trait itself — custom impls can partition by
arbitrary logic (e.g. numeric range, string prefix, etc.).

[§](https://docs.rs#shard-selection)Shard selection

The shard index is derived from the upper 32 bits of the returned hash:
`(hash >> 32) & shard_mask`. [ DefaultShardHasher](https://docs.rs/struct.DefaultShardHasher.html) (ahash when the

`ahash`
feature is enabled, otherwise std `RandomState`) produces high-quality bits
in both halves. Custom implementations should ensure the
**upper**32 bits are well-distributed across keys, not just the lower bits.

[§](https://docs.rs#warning-zero-upper-bits-route-everything-to-shard-0)Warning: zero upper bits route everything to shard 0

If `shard_hash` returns a value whose upper 32 bits are always zero, every key
will land on shard 0, defeating the purpose of sharding entirely. A common
mistake is returning a bare integer identity:

```
use cached::ShardHasher;
// BAD — `key as u64` for small integer keys leaves bits 32-63 all zero.
// All entries land on shard 0 regardless of the configured shard count.
struct IdentityHasher;
impl ShardHasher<u32> for IdentityHasher {
    fn shard_hash(&self, key: &u32) -> u64 {
        *key as u64  // upper 32 bits are always 0!
    }
}
```
Always mix or multiply the value so entropy is spread into the upper 32 bits.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use cached::ShardHasher;
/// Distributes `u64` keys using Fibonacci hashing (`key * 2^64/φ`).
/// Ensures the upper 32 bits (used for shard selection) are well-distributed.
struct FibHasher;
impl ShardHasher<u64> for FibHasher {
    fn shard_hash(&self, key: &u64) -> u64 {
        key.wrapping_mul(0x9e3779b97f4a7c15)
    }
}
```
The `'static` bound is required because the hasher is stored inside `Arc<Inner>`,
and the `Arc` is cloned across threads — a borrowed or lifetime-parameterized hasher
would prevent the cache from being `'static` and therefore from being shared via
`thread::spawn` or stored in a `static`.

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait **is** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

Concurrent analogue of [ CloneCached](https://docs.rs/trait.CloneCached.html) for the internally-synchronized sharded stores.

Like [ CloneCached](https://docs.rs/trait.CloneCached.html),

[returns a present-but-expired entry](https://docs.rs/trait.ConcurrentCloneCached.html#tymethod.cache_get_with_expiry_status)

`cache_get_with_expiry_status`**without removing it**, so callers (e.g.

[) can fall back to the stale value if a refresh fails. Takes](https://docs.rs/attr.concurrent_cached.html)

`result_fallback``&self` instead of `&mut self` because sharded stores are
internally synchronized and never need exclusive ownership from the caller.Implemented by the four expiry-capable sharded stores:
[ ShardedTtlCache](https://docs.rs/stores/sharded/type.ShardedTtlCache.html),

[,](https://docs.rs/stores/sharded/type.ShardedLruTtlCache.html)

`ShardedLruTtlCache`[, and](https://docs.rs/stores/sharded/type.ShardedExpiringCache.html)

`ShardedExpiringCache`[. Non-expiry stores (](https://docs.rs/stores/sharded/type.ShardedExpiringLruCache.html)

`ShardedExpiringLruCache`[,](https://docs.rs/stores/sharded/type.ShardedCache.html)

`ShardedCache`[) do not implement this trait, mirroring how](https://docs.rs/stores/sharded/type.ShardedLruCache.html)

`ShardedLruCache`[is absent on](https://docs.rs/trait.CloneCached.html)

`CloneCached`[and](https://docs.rs/stores/struct.UnboundCache.html)

`UnboundCache`[.](https://docs.rs/stores/struct.LruCache.html)

`LruCache`**Why  &K instead of &Q (Borrow<Q>)**: same reason as

[— the concurrent cache trait family includes external stores that must serialize the key, so the trait takes](https://docs.rs/trait.ConcurrentCached.html)

`ConcurrentCached``&K` directly rather than a generic `Borrow<Q>` that carries no
serialization guarantee.**Race window**: between the expiry check and the subsequent re-cache on `Err`, another
thread may have stored a fresh `Ok`. The re-cache will overwrite that fresh value, but
the outcome is only a redundant function call on the next expiry — not data corruption.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use cached::{ConcurrentCached, ConcurrentCloneCached, ShardedTtlCache};
use cached::time::Duration;
let c = ShardedTtlCache::builder().ttl(Duration::from_secs(60)).build().unwrap();
c.cache_set("k".to_string(), 1_i32).expect("infallible ShardedTtlCache set");
assert_eq!(c.cache_get_with_expiry_status(&"k".to_string()), (Some(1_i32), false)); // live
assert_eq!(c.cache_get_with_expiry_status(&"x".to_string()), (None, false));        // absent
// a present-but-expired entry yields (Some(v), true)
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cached/lib.rs.html#1061)#### fn [cache_get_with_expiry_status](https://docs.rs#tymethod.cache_get_with_expiry_status)(&self, key: [&K](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)) -> ([Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<V>, [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cached/lib.rs.html#1061)

#### fn [cache_get_with_expiry_status](https://docs.rs#tymethod.cache_get_with_expiry_status)(&self, key: [&K](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)) -> ([Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<V>, [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

Look up a cached value and report whether the found entry is expired.

Returns `(value, expired)` where:

- `(None, false)`— key not present
- `(Some(v), false)`— key present and live (hits counter incremented)
- `(Some(v), true)`— key present but expired; the stale value is returned so callers can fall back to it if a refresh fails. The entry is- **not**removed from the cache and eviction counters are- **not**incremented (misses counter incremented).

Unlike [ ConcurrentCached::cache_get](https://docs.rs/trait.ConcurrentCached.html#tymethod.cache_get), this never removes an expired entry — it
intentionally leaves it in place so it can be returned as a stale fallback. Expired
entries are swept by a subsequent

`cache_get`, an explicit `cache_remove`, or `evict()`.## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait **is** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# ExpiringLruCache in cached::stores - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cached/2.0.2/cached/stores/struct.ExpiringLruCache.html

## Expand description

LRU-bounded cache with per-value expiry.

Stores values that implement the [ Expires](https://docs.rs/trait.Expires.html) trait so that expiration
is determined by the values themselves. This is useful for caching
values which themselves contain an expiry timestamp.

For an unbounded variant (no size cap), see [ ExpiringCache](https://docs.rs/struct.ExpiringCache.html).
When using the

`#[cached]` proc macro, `expires = true` selects this store when `max_size`
is also specified; without `max_size`, it selects the unbounded `ExpiringCache`.Note: This cache is in-memory only.

Note: once specialization is stable (`#[feature(specialization)]`), the expiry-checking
behavior here could be folded into [ LruCache](https://docs.rs/struct.LruCache.html) via a specialized

`Cached<K, V>` impl
for `V: Expires`, eliminating this separate type. Until then, the two must remain
distinct because overlapping blanket impls are not allowed on stable Rust.## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

#### pub fn [cache_clear_with_on_evict](https://docs.rs#method.cache_clear_with_on_evict)(&mut self)

Remove all entries and fire the `on_evict` callback for each one, incrementing the
evictions counter.

Unlike [ cache_clear](https://docs.rs/trait.Cached.html#tymethod.cache_clear) (which removes entries silently),
this method invokes

`on_evict` for every removed entry (whether or not they had expired)
and increments `evictions`. If no `on_evict` callback was configured, it falls back to
the plain `cache_clear`.## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

# ExpiringCache in cached::stores - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cached/2.0.2/cached/stores/struct.ExpiringCache.html

## Expand description

Size-unbounded cache where each value controls its own expiry via [ Expires](https://docs.rs/trait.Expires.html).

Unlike [ TtlCache](https://docs.rs/struct.TtlCache.html) which applies a single global TTL duration to
all entries,

`ExpiringCache` has **no global TTL**. Each value determines its own expiration by implementing

[. The store checks](https://docs.rs/trait.Expires.html)

`Expires``is_expired()` on every lookup and evicts
expired entries on access.For a size-bounded variant that also evicts by LRU, see [ ExpiringLruCache](https://docs.rs/struct.ExpiringLruCache.html).
When using the

`#[cached]` proc macro, `expires = true` automatically selects this store
(or `ExpiringLruCache` when `size` is also specified).[§](https://docs.rs#memory-note)Memory note

`ExpiringCache` is **unbounded** and only removes expired entries when the same key is
accessed again. Entries that expire and are never re-fetched stay in memory indefinitely.
For high-cardinality workloads, call [ evict()](https://docs.rs/struct.ExpiringCache.html#method.evict) periodically to
sweep and remove all expired entries, or prefer

[with a](https://docs.rs/struct.ExpiringLruCache.html)

`ExpiringLruCache``size` bound to cap memory usage automatically.```
use cached::{Cached, Expires, ExpiringCache};
struct Token {
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    value: String,
    expired: bool,
}
impl Expires for Token {
    fn is_expired(&self) -> bool { self.expired }
}
let mut cache: ExpiringCache<u32, Token> = ExpiringCache::builder().build().unwrap();
cache.cache_set(1, Token { value: "live".into(), expired: false });
assert!(cache.cache_get(&1).is_some());
cache.cache_set(2, Token { value: "stale".into(), expired: true });
assert!(cache.cache_get(&2).is_none()); // expired → not returned
```
Note: This cache is in-memory only.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Evict all expired entries from the cache.

Returns the number of entries removed. Fires the `on_evict` callback for each
removed entry. Use this periodically for high-cardinality workloads to reclaim
memory from entries that expire but are never re-accessed.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cached/stores/expiring.rs.html#196-210)#### pub fn [cache_clear_with_on_evict](https://docs.rs#method.cache_clear_with_on_evict)(&mut self)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cached/stores/expiring.rs.html#196-210)

#### pub fn [cache_clear_with_on_evict](https://docs.rs#method.cache_clear_with_on_evict)(&mut self)

Remove all entries and fire the `on_evict` callback for each one, incrementing the
evictions counter.

Unlike [ cache_clear](https://docs.rs/trait.Cached.html#tymethod.cache_clear) (which removes entries silently),
this method invokes

`on_evict` for every removed entry (whether or not they had expired)
and increments `evictions`. If no `on_evict` callback was configured, it falls back to
the plain `cache_clear`.## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

# Expires in cached::stores - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cached/2.0.2/cached/stores/trait.Expires.html

```
pub trait Expires {
    // Required method
    fn
```
[is_expired](https://docs.rs#tymethod.is_expired)(&self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html);
}## Expand description

Implemented by values stored in [ ExpiringLruCache](https://docs.rs/struct.ExpiringLruCache.html) and

[so the value itself decides when it is stale. Expired values are not returned by lookups and are removed on access:](https://docs.rs/struct.ExpiringCache.html)

`ExpiringCache````
use cached::{Cached, Expires, ExpiringCache, ExpiringLruCache};
struct Token {
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    value: String,
    expired: bool,
}
impl Expires for Token {
    fn is_expired(&self) -> bool {
        self.expired
    }
}
// Unbounded store (default for `#[cached(expires = true)]`)
let mut cache: ExpiringCache<u32, Token> = ExpiringCache::builder().build().unwrap();
cache.cache_set(1, Token { value: "live".into(), expired: false });
assert!(cache.cache_get(&1).is_some());
cache.cache_set(2, Token { value: "stale".into(), expired: true });
assert!(cache.cache_get(&2).is_none()); // expired -> not returned
// LRU-bounded store (`#[cached(expires = true, size = N)]`)
let mut lru: ExpiringLruCache<u32, Token> = ExpiringLruCache::builder().max_size(8).build().unwrap();
lru.cache_set(3, Token { value: "live".into(), expired: false });
assert!(lru.cache_get(&3).is_some());
```

# CacheEvict in cached::stores - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cached/2.0.2/cached/stores/trait.CacheEvict.html

## Expand description

Trait for cache stores that support explicit eviction of expired entries.

Implementors remove all entries that are past their expiry from the store and
invoke the `on_evict` callback (if configured) for each removed entry.

This trait is for in-memory stores with infallible expiration checks. IO-backed
stores expose their own APIs because sweeping can fail: `DiskCache` uses
`remove_expired_entries`, while Redis relies on server-side key expiry.

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

Remove all expired entries from the cache, returning the number removed.

Fires the `on_evict` callback and increments `cache_evictions()` for each removed entry.
Hit/miss metrics are not affected; call [ cache_reset_metrics](https://docs.rs/trait.Cached.html#method.cache_reset_metrics)
separately if needed.

**Note for sharded in-memory stores**: the concrete types expose an inherent `evict(&self)`
method that does not require `&mut self`. When you hold only a shared reference (e.g., via
`Arc`), call the inherent method directly instead of going through this trait.

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait **is** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

`async` and (crate features `redis_connection_manager` or `redis_smol` or `redis_tokio`)Set the namespace for cache keys. Defaults to `cached-redis-store:`.
Used to generate keys formatted as: `{namespace}:{prefix}:{key}`.
Empty namespace values are omitted from the generated key.

**Note:** colons in the namespace are not escaped. A namespace containing
an interior colon (e.g. `"a:b"`) can produce keys that collide with a
shorter namespace combined with a prefix (e.g. namespace `"a"`, prefix `"b"`).

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cached/stores/redis.rs.html#703-706)**crate feature **`async` and (crate features `redis_connection_manager` or `redis_smol` or `redis_tokio`) only.

Used to generate keys formatted as: `{namespace}:{prefix}:{key}`.
Empty prefix values are omitted from the generated key.

**Note:** colons in the prefix are not escaped and can cause key collisions
with differently-split namespace/prefix combinations sharing the same segments.

# ExpiringCacheBuilder in cached::stores - Rust

`pub struct ExpiringCacheBuilder<K, V: `[Expires](https://docs.rs/trait.Expires.html)> { /* private fields */ }## Expand description

Builder for [ ExpiringCache](https://docs.rs/struct.ExpiringCache.html).

Note: there is intentionally **no  .ttl() setter**. An

`ExpiringCache` has no global
expiry duration — each value decides when it is expired via the [trait. For a single global TTL applied to every entry, use](https://docs.rs/trait.Expires.html)

`Expires`[or](https://docs.rs/struct.TtlCache.html)

`TtlCache`[instead.](https://docs.rs/struct.LruTtlCache.html)

`LruTtlCache`## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cached/stores/expiring.rs.html#105-156)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-ExpiringCacheBuilder%3CK,+V%3E)### impl<K, V: [Expires](https://docs.rs/trait.Expires.html)> [ExpiringCacheBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.ExpiringCacheBuilder.html)<K, V>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cached/stores/expiring.rs.html#105-156)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-ExpiringCacheBuilder%3CK,+V%3E)

### impl<K, V: [Expires](https://docs.rs/trait.Expires.html)> [ExpiringCacheBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.ExpiringCacheBuilder.html)<K, V>

Set a callback to be invoked when an entry is removed from the cache.

The callback fires when an expired value is encountered during `cache_get`,
`cache_get_mut`, `cache_get_or_set_with`, `cache_try_get_or_set_with`,
their async equivalents, an explicit `evict()` sweep, or an explicit
`cache_remove` (including when the removed entry was already expired).
It does **not** fire on `cache_clear` or `cache_reset` (consistent with
[ ExpiringLruCache](https://docs.rs/struct.ExpiringLruCache.html)).
Use

[instead of](https://docs.rs/struct.ExpiringCache.html#method.cache_clear_with_on_evict)

`cache_clear_with_on_evict`[to opt into callback firing and eviction counter increments when clearing all entries.](https://docs.rs/trait.Cached.html#tymethod.cache_clear)

`cache_clear`## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

Least Recently Used / `Sized` Cache

evictions counter.

this method invokes

# ShardedCache in cached::stores::sharded - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cached/2.0.2/cached/stores/sharded/type.ShardedCache.html

`pub type ShardedCache<K, V> = `[ShardedCacheBase](https://docs.rs/struct.ShardedCacheBase.html)<K, V, [DefaultShardHasher](https://docs.rs/struct.DefaultShardHasher.html)>;## Expand description

A fully-concurrent, partitioned, unbounded in-memory cache.

Wraps an `Arc` — `clone()` is an Arc-share (shared state), not a deep copy.
Use [ deep_clone](https://docs.rs/struct.ShardedCacheBase.html#method.deep_clone) to get an independent copy.

**Note**: reads return owned values cloned from under the shard lock, so `V` must
implement `Clone`.

This is a type alias for `ShardedCacheBase<K, V, DefaultShardHasher>`.
To use a custom shard hasher, construct a [ ShardedCacheBase](https://docs.rs/struct.ShardedCacheBase.html) directly via

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.ShardedCacheBase.html#method.builder)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cached/stores/sharded/unbound.rs.html#121-147)#### pub fn [deep_clone](https://docs.rs#method.deep_clone)(&self) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cached/stores/sharded/unbound.rs.html#121-147)

#### pub fn [deep_clone](https://docs.rs#method.deep_clone)(&self) -> Self

Return an independent deep copy of this cache — entries and metrics are
duplicated, not shared. In most cases [ Clone::clone](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/clone/trait.Clone.html#tymethod.clone) (Arc-share) is
what you want.

```
use cached::{ConcurrentCached, ShardedCache};
let cache: ShardedCache<String, u32> = ShardedCache::builder().build().unwrap();
cache.cache_set("k".to_string(), 1).expect("ShardedCache operations are infallible");
let shared = cache.clone();     // Arc clone — same backing store
let deep   = cache.deep_clone(); // independent snapshot
cache.cache_set("k".to_string(), 2).expect("ShardedCache operations are infallible");
assert_eq!(shared.cache_get(&"k".to_string()).expect("ShardedCache operations are infallible"), Some(2)); // sees update
assert_eq!(deep.cache_get(&"k".to_string()).expect("ShardedCache operations are infallible"),   Some(1)); // snapshot unchanged
```

#### pub fn [cache_clear_with_on_evict](https://docs.rs#method.cache_clear_with_on_evict)(&self)

Remove all entries from every shard, firing `on_evict` for each removed entry when a
callback is configured.

If no `on_evict` callback is configured, this is equivalent to [ clear](https://docs.rs/struct.ShardedCacheBase.html#method.clear).

**Note:** `ShardedCache` does not track eviction counts — `metrics().evictions` always
returns `None` regardless of whether `on_evict` fires.

### impl<K, V, H> [ShardedCacheBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.ShardedCacheBuilder.html)<K, V, H>

Set the number of shards (rounded up to the next power of two).

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cached/stores/sharded/unbound.rs.html#357-365)#### pub fn [hasher](https://docs.rs#method.hasher)<H2: [ShardHasher](https://docs.rs/trait.ShardHasher.html)<K>>(
    self,
    hasher: H2,
) -> [ShardedCacheBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.ShardedCacheBuilder.html)<K, V, H2>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cached/stores/sharded/unbound.rs.html#357-365)

#### pub fn [hasher](https://docs.rs#method.hasher)<H2: [ShardHasher](https://docs.rs/trait.ShardHasher.html)<K>>(
    self,
    hasher: H2,
) -> [ShardedCacheBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.ShardedCacheBuilder.html)<K, V, H2>

Set a custom shard-selection hasher, changing the type parameter.

The hasher decides only which shard a key maps to — it does **not** replace the
per-shard store’s own internal hashing. Shard selection reads the **upper 32 bits**
of the returned hash (`(hash >> 32) & shard_mask`), so a custom [ ShardHasher](https://docs.rs/trait.ShardHasher.html) must
distribute keys across those high bits to avoid lopsided shards; a hasher that only
varies the low 32 bits will pile every key into one shard. See

[for the distribution contract and a worked example. Defaults to](https://docs.rs/trait.ShardHasher.html)

`ShardHasher`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.DefaultShardHasher.html)

`DefaultShardHasher`Set a callback invoked when an entry is explicitly removed via
[ cache_remove](https://docs.rs/trait.ConcurrentCached.html#tymethod.cache_remove) or

[. Does](https://docs.rs/trait.ConcurrentCached.html#tymethod.cache_remove_entry)

`cache_remove_entry`**not**fire on

[; use](https://docs.rs/struct.ShardedCacheBase.html#method.clear)

`clear`[to opt in.](https://docs.rs/struct.ShardedCacheBase.html#method.cache_clear_with_on_evict)

`cache_clear_with_on_evict`**Note**: `ShardedCache` does not track eviction counts — `metrics().evictions` always
returns `None` even when `on_evict` is configured. Use the callback itself to count
evictions if needed.

The closure must be `'static` (its captures cannot borrow from the local stack), but `K`
and `V` themselves are not required to be `'static`.

Build the cache.

Use [ ShardedCache::builder()](https://docs.rs/struct.ShardedCacheBase.html#method.builder) (or

[) to obtain a builder, configure it, then call](https://docs.rs/struct.ShardedCacheBase.html#method.builder)

`ShardedCacheBase::builder()``.build()`.This builder never fails for valid inputs. The only error case is an
invalid shard count (e.g. `usize::MAX` overflows the next-power-of-two
rounding).

`shards` count overflows
when rounded up to the next power of two.[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cached/stores/sharded/unbound.rs.html#437-459)#### pub fn [copy_from](https://docs.rs#method.copy_from)<H2: [ShardHasher](https://docs.rs/trait.ShardHasher.html)<K>>(
    self,

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cached/stores/sharded/unbound.rs.html#437-459)

#### pub fn [copy_from](https://docs.rs#method.copy_from)<H2: [ShardHasher](https://docs.rs/trait.ShardHasher.html)<K>>(
    self,
    existing: &[ShardedCacheBase](https://docs.rs/struct.ShardedCacheBase.html)<K, V, H2>,
) -> [ShardedCacheBase](https://docs.rs/struct.ShardedCacheBase.html)<K, V, H>

Build the new cache and copy every entry from `existing` into it.

Entries are re-hashed through `H` so they land in the correct shards
of the new cache. Acquires each shard’s read lock on `existing` one at
a time — `existing` keeps serving concurrent ops throughout.

Swapping which cache is “live” after the copy is the caller’s responsibility. Requests racing the swap may observe a cache miss.

**Note**: writes to `existing` that occur after a shard’s read lock is
released may or may not appear in the new cache; the new cache warms up
from misses after the swap.

**Note**: `on_evict` callbacks on `existing` do not fire — entries are read
(not removed) from the source cache.

# ShardedExpiringCacheBuilder in cached::stores::sharded - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cached/2.0.2/cached/stores/sharded/struct.ShardedExpiringCacheBuilder.html

`pub struct ShardedExpiringCacheBuilder<K, V: `[Expires](https://docs.rs/trait.Expires.html), H = [DefaultShardHasher](https://docs.rs/struct.DefaultShardHasher.html)> { /* private fields */ }## Expand description

Builder for [ ShardedExpiringCacheBase](https://docs.rs/struct.ShardedExpiringCacheBase.html).

Note: there is intentionally **no  .ttl() setter**. A sharded expiring cache has no global
expiry duration — each value decides when it is expired via the

[trait. For a single global TTL applied to every entry, use](https://docs.rs/trait.Expires.html)

`Expires`[or](https://docs.rs/type.ShardedTtlCache.html)

`ShardedTtlCache`[instead.](https://docs.rs/type.ShardedLruTtlCache.html)

`ShardedLruTtlCache`## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

### impl<K, V: [Expires](https://docs.rs/trait.Expires.html), H> [ShardedExpiringCacheBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.ShardedExpiringCacheBuilder.html)<K, V, H>

Set the number of shards (rounded up to the next power of two).

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cached/stores/sharded/expiring.rs.html#467-475)#### pub fn [hasher](https://docs.rs#method.hasher)<H2: [ShardHasher](https://docs.rs/trait.ShardHasher.html)<K>>(
    self,
    hasher: H2,
) -> [ShardedExpiringCacheBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.ShardedExpiringCacheBuilder.html)<K, V, H2>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cached/stores/sharded/expiring.rs.html#467-475)

#### pub fn [hasher](https://docs.rs#method.hasher)<H2: [ShardHasher](https://docs.rs/trait.ShardHasher.html)<K>>(
    self,
    hasher: H2,
) -> [ShardedExpiringCacheBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.ShardedExpiringCacheBuilder.html)<K, V, H2>

Set a custom shard-selection hasher, changing the type parameter.

The hasher decides only which shard a key maps to — it does **not** replace the
per-shard store’s own internal hashing. Shard selection reads the **upper 32 bits**
of the returned hash (`(hash >> 32) & shard_mask`), so a custom [ ShardHasher](https://docs.rs/trait.ShardHasher.html) must
distribute keys across those high bits to avoid lopsided shards; a hasher that only
varies the low 32 bits will pile every key into one shard. See

[for the distribution contract and a worked example. Defaults to](https://docs.rs/trait.ShardHasher.html)

`ShardHasher`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.DefaultShardHasher.html)

Build the new cache and copy every non-expired entry from `existing` into it.

Acquires each shard’s read lock on `existing` one at a time — `existing`
keeps serving concurrent ops throughout. Entries whose
[ is_expired](https://docs.rs/trait.Expires.html#tymethod.is_expired) returns

`true` at copy time are
skipped and not transferred.**Note**: `on_evict` callbacks on `existing` do not fire — entries are read
(not removed) from the source cache.

#### pub fn [metrics](https://docs.rs#method.metrics)(&self) -> [CacheMetrics](https://docs.rs/struct.CacheMetrics.html)

Return aggregate metrics across all shards.

`evictions` aggregates every entry removal that fires (or would fire) `on_evict`,
across all shards:

- LRU capacity evictions during `cache_set`
- explicit removes via `cache_remove``cache_remove_entry`
- bulk removal via `cache_clear_with_on_evict`**not**`clear`
- expired entries dropped lazily on access during
`cache_get`
- expired entries swept by `evict`

`capacity` reflects the effective total capacity — may exceed the requested
`size` when the 16-per-shard minimum floor is applied; see [ capacity](https://docs.rs/struct.ShardedExpiringLruCacheBase.html#method.capacity).
